verses.text: Masters, treat your enslaved workers justly and fairly. Remember that you also have a Master in heaven.
Keep praying faithfully. Stay alert, and give thanks.
At the same time, pray for us too, that God will open a door for our message so we can share the mystery of Christ, for which I'm in chains.
Pray that I'll make it clear, as I should.
Be wise in the way you act toward outsiders, making the most of every opportunity.
Let your words always be gracious and thoughtful, so you'll know how to answer each person.
Tychicus, our dear brother, faithful servant, and fellow worker in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
I sent him for this very reason: so you can know how we're doing, and so he can encourage your hearts.
Onesimus is coming with him. He's a faithful and dearly loved brother, one of your own. They'll tell you everything that's happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends greetings, as does Mark, Barnabas' cousin. You've received instructions about him: welcome him if he comes to you.
Jesus, who is called Justus, sends greetings too. These are the only fellow workers for God's Kingdom from the circumcised group who have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, one of your own and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, asking that you'll stand firm, mature, and fully confident in everything God wants.
I can testify that he works hard for you, and for the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, our dear doctor, and Demas send greetings.
Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church that meets in her home.
After this letter has been read among you, make sure it's read in the church in Laodicea too. And you should read the letter from Laodicea.
Tell Archippus, ‘Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, and carry it out.’
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember that I'm in chains. Grace be with you. Amen.
